questions.context: Amines are usually formed from nitro compounds, halides, amides, imides, etc. They exhibit hydrogen bonding which influences their physical properties. In alkyl amines, a combination of electron releasing, steric and hydrogen bonding factors influence the stability of the substituted ammonium cations in protic polar solvents and thus affect the basic nature of amines. In aromatic amines, electron releasing and withdrawing groups, respectively increase and decrease their basic character. Influence of the number of hydrogen atoms at nitrogen atom on the type of reactions and nature of products is responsible for identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Presence of amino group in aromatic ring enhances reactivity of the aromatic amines. Aryl diazonium salts provide advantageous methods for producing aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes by reductive removal of the diazo group.

In alkyl amines, a combination of electron releasing, steric and hydrogen bonding factors influence the stability of the substituted ammonium cations in protic polar solvents and thus affect the basic nature of amines. In aromatic amines, electron releasing and withdrawing groups, respectively increase and decrease their basic character. Influence of the number of hydrogen atoms at nitrogen atom on the type of reactions and nature of products is responsible for identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Presence of amino group in aromatic ring enhances reactivity of the aromatic amines. Aryl diazonium salts provide advantageous methods for producing aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes by reductive removal of the diazo group.
questions.stem: An aromatic compound 'A' of molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_7H_6O_2}\) on treatment with aqueous ammonia and heating forms compound 'B'. Compound 'B' on heating with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) and aqueous KOH gives a compound 'C' of molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_6H_7N}\). Write the structures of A, B and C.

questions.stem:
Complete the following reactions giving main products :
(1) Aniline \(+\ \mathrm{Br_2\,(aq)} \longrightarrow\)
(2) Benzenediazonium chloride \(\xrightarrow[\mathrm{(ii)\ NaNO_2/Cu,\ \Delta}]{\mathrm{(i)\ HBF_4}}\)
questions._flag: Sub-part (1) is bromination of aniline and belongs to 'Chemical Reactions of Amines'; (2) is the Balz-Schiemann reaction of a diazonium salt. A 1:1 split, filed on 'Chemical Reactions of Diazonium Salts' because that is what the passage's closing sentence sets up. Printed marks notation is '2 x 1 = 2'.
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE — Both reactants are DRAWN, not named: (1) is a benzene ring bearing —NH2 and (2) is a benzene ring bearing —N2(+) Cl(-), each followed by its printed reagent arrow. The stem above names them in words (aniline, benzenediazonium chloride), which is what the drawings show, but the printed reaction block should be attached as the crop. Page idx 18, upper third.

questions.context:
Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules like carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, etc. Carbohydrates are optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones or molecules which provide such units on hydrolysis. They are broadly classified into three groups — monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. Monosaccharides are held together by glycosidic linkages to form disaccharides like sucrose, maltose or polysaccharides like starch and cellulose.

Another biomolecule : proteins are polymers of \(\alpha\)-amino acids which are linked by peptide bonds. Ten amino acids are called essential amino acids. Structure and shape of proteins can be studied at four different levels i.e. primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary, each level being more complex than the previous one.
questions.stem: What is the difference between a glycosidic linkage and peptide linkage ?
questions._flag: The question spans two subtopics by construction — the glycosidic linkage is taught under 'Carbohydrates' and the peptide linkage under 'Proteins'. Filed on Proteins because the marking scheme's value points LEAD with the peptide linkage and define it precisely (a —CONH— bond), which is the half a candidate has to state exactly.

questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.stem:
(a) Draw structure of the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone of benzaldehyde.
(b) Which acid of the following pair is a stronger acid ?
(c) Write the chemical equation involved in Rosenmund's reduction.
(d) Why are \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms of aldehydes and ketones acidic in nature ?
(e) Write a chemical test to distinguish between Benzaldehyde and Benzoic acid.
questions._flag: Sub-part (b) is acid strength and belongs to 'Chemical Reactions of Carboxylic Acids'; (c) Rosenmund's reduction belongs to 'Preparation of Aldehydes and Ketones'; (a), (d) and (e) are aldehyde/ketone chemistry, so the row is filed on 'Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones' on the 3:2 split. Printed marks notation is '5 x 1 = 5'. Q33 carries NO internal choice, which is consistent with instruction (viii)'s count of two for Section E, both of which (Q34, Q35) are printed OR blocks.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — REQUIRED for sub-part (b), which is unanswerable from its text alone: the pair is printed ONLY as two drawn para-disubstituted benzene rings joined by the word 'or' — the left ring bears —CF3 and —COOH, the right bears —CH3 and —COOH — and the stem names neither compound. Naming them would state the answer, since the question is exactly which substituent makes the acid stronger. Page idx 20, immediately under sub-part (b).

questions.stem:
(i) Calculate the emf of the following cell at 298 K :
\(\mathrm{Al\,(s)} \mid \mathrm{Al}^{3+}\,(0{\cdot}001\ \mathrm{M}) \parallel \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\,(0{\cdot}1\ \mathrm{M}) \mid \mathrm{Ni\,(s)}\)
[Given : \(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Al}^{3+}/\mathrm{Al}} = -\,1{\cdot}66\) V, \(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}/\mathrm{Ni}} = -\,0{\cdot}25\) V, log 10 = 1]
(ii) With the help of a graph explain why it is not possible to determine \(\Lambda^{\circ}_{\mathrm{m}}\) for a weak electrolyte by extrapolating the molar conductivity \((\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}})\) versus \(\mathrm{C}^{1/2}\) curve as for strong electrolyte.
questions._flag: Sub-part (ii) is 'Conductance of Electrolytic Solutions' (2 marks); the row is filed on 'Nernst Equation' for the 3-mark part (i), which is the larger half by the printed 3 + 2 = 5 split. The graph in (ii) is what the CANDIDATE must draw, so this is not a figure dependency.

questions.stem:
(i) The molar conductivities of \(\mathrm{NH_4^{+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\) ion are \(73{\cdot}8\) S \(\mathrm{cm^2\ mol^{-1}}\) and \(76{\cdot}2\) S \(\mathrm{cm^2\ mol^{-1}}\) respectively. The conductivity of \(0{\cdot}1\) M \(\mathrm{NH_4Cl}\) is \(1{\cdot}29 \times 10^{-2}\) S \(\mathrm{cm^{-1}}\). Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation.
(ii) Calculate the half-cell potential at 298 K for the reaction
\(\mathrm{Zn}^{2+} + 2\mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}\)
if \([\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}] = 0{\cdot}1\) M and \(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}/\mathrm{Zn}} = -\,0{\cdot}76\) V.
questions._flag: Sub-part (ii) is 'Nernst Equation' (2 marks); the row is filed on 'Conductance of Electrolytic Solutions' for the 3-mark part (i), per the printed 3 + 2 = 5 split.

questions.stem:

(1) \(\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}\) salts are colourless while \(\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\) salts are coloured.
(2) \(\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}\) is a strong reducing agent.
(3) Transition metals and their compounds show catalytic activities.
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidizing action of \(\mathrm{MnO_4^{-}}\) in acidic medium with
(1) \(\mathrm{I^{-}}\) ion, and
(2) \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) ion.
questions._flag: Sub-part (ii) is permanganate chemistry and belongs to 'Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements' (2 marks); the row is filed on 'General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)' for the 3-mark part (i) — colour, reducing character and catalytic activity — per the printed 3 + 2 = 5 split.

(i) Name two oxometal anions of the 3d series of the transition metals in which the metal exhibits the oxidation state equal to its group number.
(ii) What is the effect of increasing pH on a solution of \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\) ?
(iii) Why is \(\mathrm{Cu^{+}}\) not stable in aqueous solution ?
(iv) Name a member of Lanthanoid series which is well-known to exhibit +4 oxidation state.
(v) Name two elements of 3d series which show anomalous electronic configuration.
questions._flag: The five printed 1-mark sub-parts spread across four subtopics — (i) and (ii) 'Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements', (iii) 'General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)', (iv) 'The Lanthanoids', (v) 'Electronic Configurations of the d-Block Elements'. Filed on the 2-mark plurality. Printed marks notation is '5 x 1 = 5'.
